overview: Nigeria is one of Africa's densest femtech and women's-health-tech ecosystems, home to roughly 29% of the continent's top healthtech innovators and a heavy concentration of women-led ventures spanning maternal health, sexual and reproductive health, and menstrual care. The sector added dozens of startups since COVID-19 (128 active healthtech firms by 2026) and benefits from real policy momentum, including a national Safe Motherhood Strategy (2024-2028) and six clinical guidelines launched in 2025. However, dedicated venture capital remains thin: healthtech funding collapsed to only a few million dollars in 2025, leaving women founders heavily reliant on grants and gender-lens vehicles like Aruwa Capital, FirstCheck Africa, IFC's She Wins Africa, and UNICEF Femtech Ventures.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: The last 18 months saw new global and pan-African femtech programs reach Nigerian founders, alongside sobering funding-decline data.

items.text: TechCabal Insights' State of Healthtech in Nigeria 2026 report finds Nigeria added 65 healthtech startups after COVID-19 (128 active total), many in maternal and reproductive care.
Technext profiles 8 Nigerian women's healthtech startups and founders reshaping maternal and reproductive care.
Nigerian maternal-health startup HelpMum selected among 18 grantees for ICONIQ Impact's $100M Child Survival portfolio.
UNICEF Femtech Ventures backs 11 startups across Africa and Asia (incl. Nigeria's Natal Cares and Whispa) with up to $100k equity-free each; cohort activated in Pretoria.
IFC and ASR Africa expand She Wins Africa from 100 to 1,000 women entrepreneurs after pilot mobilised over $4M in startup financing.
Big Family 360 Foundation launches HerPride, a cycle-tracking and sanitary-product access app for Nigerian women.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Nigeria carries roughly 20% of global maternal and child deaths, and in 2025 the federal government launched an unusually deep set of maternal and reproductive health policies.

items.text: Federal Government commits to cutting maternal mortality by 20% by 2027 under the Health Sector Renewal Initiative.

Health Minister Muhammad Pate unveils six national policy documents on Safe Motherhood Day, including the Safe Motherhood Strategy (2024-2028) and clinical guidelines for postpartum haemorrhage and hypertensive disorders.
Nigeria launches Strategic Directions for Nursing and Midwifery 2025-2030 to expand maternal-care workforce capacity.
National Guidelines on Self-Care for Sexual, Reproductive and Maternal Health target 30% uptake of self-care interventions (foundational SRH policy).

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Nigeria concentrates a large share of Africa's women-led healthtech, with activity clustered in maternal, sexual/reproductive, and menstrual health.

items.text: Nigeria hosts ~29% of Africa's top healthtech innovators; 76% of solely women-founded health-supply-chain companies are based in Nigeria and South Africa.
Whispa Health reaches 30,000+ users with anonymous SRH teleconsultations, STI test kits and contraceptive delivery.
HelpMum scales AI-driven maternal and infant health / vaccine-delivery interventions across Nigerian communities.
Nigeria's telemedicine sector is growing again as digital pharmacies, diagnostics and maternal care expand.
19-year-old Nigerian innovator launches Period Padi, a menstrual-health nonprofit with cycle tracking and school wellness booths, funded by ~$38k in grants ahead of a 2026 rollout.

sections.heading: Notable funding rounds
sections.narrative: Dedicated venture money is scarce, so Nigerian women's-health founders lean on grants, accelerators and gender-lens funds rather than priced equity rounds.
